name: Ruslan Adeyinka
description: Tatar-Yoruba; twenty years brokering structured salvage of failing aerostatic stock for AshgraveMaterials. Has watched three blocs ride into The Low and knows exactly what scavenger salvage looks like when it reaches a bloc that still has people on it. His offer to Candelaria is his conscience wearing a contract. Dresses one bracket below his income so rooms don't harden against him. Carries the deconstruction schedules of his last three blocs in his case and will show them to anyone who asks — the tidy ones, and the one that wasn't.
narration_voice: Seen only through Teo's POV. Speaks in offers and floors, never threats.

core_fears: Arriving at a bloc six months after his offer was refused and finding what the scavengers left
Becoming the kind of broker who stops making the offer in person
core_desires: To close Candelaria clean — everyone relocated, everything reclaimed, nobody on it when it goes
To be understood as the alternative to the fall, not the push
coping_mechanisms: Showing the numbers again, slower, when refused — he believes refusal is always an information problem
Walking a bloc's commons before making an offer so his model has a face on it
blind_spots: His model prices the bloc's community at zero because it has no column for it — he never learns this on the page
He reads Dagny Obuya's refusal to negotiate as denial rather than as an answer
psychology.secret: The third bloc — the one that wasn't tidy — refused him twice before it dropped into The Low. He keeps its deconstruction schedule in his case with the others, though there was nothing structured about how it ended. Never disclosed on-page.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Actuarial-humane: reclamation value, relocation floor, controlled deconstruction, bracket relief. Glosses corporate terms unprompted, as courtesy.
speech_patterns.cadence: Unhurried, complete sentences, always ends on the other party's option — 'that's yours to refuse.'
verbal_tics: Puts the strongest argument against his own offer on the table before anyone else can
Never says 'salvage' inside the bloc; says 'reclamation' and knows everyone hears the difference
example_lines: I've done this three times. Twice it was on schedule. I brought all three schedules — ask me about the third.
The frame doesn't care how the vote goes. That's the only thing in this that isn't negotiable.
You can refuse me. I'd rather you refuse me knowing the number than refuse me proud.
avoidances: Never mentions Priya's daughter — he knows about her and considers using it beneath the work
Never pressures on a deadline he didn't set

story_hooks: The third bloc's schedule in his case
His standing offer as the story's honest, insufficient arithmetic
narrative_function: Antagonist-shaped but not a villain: a correct model missing a column. His arithmetic is never refuted, only answered.
